title: Committee of Supply − Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: Foreign manpower and workplace laws
sections.summary: The Fair Consideration Framework, EP salary criteria and foreign manpower tightening levelled the playing field, while WICA and WSHA were enhanced for wage changes and workplace accidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the policy front, the Fair Consideration Framework and raising of Employment Pass (EP) salary criteria and other foreign manpower tightening measures have helped level the playing field for the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Enhancements to the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) and Workplace Safety and Health Act (WSHA) have also been instituted to keep pace with wage changes and workplace accidents.

sections.label: Review of Singapore labour laws
sections.summary: MOM and tripartite partners are suggested to review the EA, IRA, ECA and Trade Unions Act, including whether to restrict EA scope to those earning under $4,500 and exclude civil servants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The new nature of the employment relationship, rising median wages, workforce profile change and diversity of work will require us to review our labour legislation to keep pace with the changes and the uncertain global outlook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, suggesting for MOM and our tripartite partners to continue its good work to carry out a review of the labour laws of Singapore − the EA, IRA, Employment Claims Act (ECA) and Trade Unions Act − to keep pace with the changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First is whether there is a need to restrict the scope of EA to those earning less than $4,500 as well as exclude civil servants from the ambit of the Act.

sections.label: Transfers under section 18A EA
sections.summary: With more mergers, acquisitions and restructuring, there is a challenge whether a transfer falls within section 18A of the EA, which allows transfer without retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, with an increasing number of mergers and acquisitions and organisational restructuring and reorganisation these days, we often face the challenge of whether a transfer falls squarely within the provisions of section 18A of the EA which allows for transfer of employees to a new entity without the need to pay retrenchment benefits.

sections.label: Freelancers joining trade unions
sections.summary: The Trade Unions Act requires a contract of service to join a union, so freelancers on contracts for service may not be full members; a workgroup is suggested to study relaxing this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: With greater complexity in the terms and conditions of work as well as cases of unfair termination of contract where workers, especially PMEs, are just given notice pay and told to leave the company, I hope the Act can keep pace with the developments and address some of these issues which may not be salary-related.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: At present, the Trade Unions Act requires a person to be in a "contract of service" to join a trade union.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Freelancers who are in a "contract for service" may not be full-fledged union members per se.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: As such, I suggest MOM form a workgroup to study this carefully and remove or relax the prohibition and explore ways to allow freelancers to be union members without compromising or contravening traditional collective bargaining and representation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The review cannot be done in silos and, in the spirit of tripartism, I ask for our tripartite partners to review and examine carefully and further strengthen our tripartite relationship in the course of doing so by bringing even more workers and companies within our fold.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: If we do not align our manpower with our economic growth strategies, given Singapore's tight labour market, manpower will become a bottleneck to economic growth.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow initiatives effectiveness
sections.summary: The Minister is asked how Adapt and Grow initiatives like CSP and PCP helped workers acquire skills and transition into 2016 jobs, and what learnings shaped Budget 2017 enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how the Adapt and Grow initiatives like Career Support Programme (CSP) and Professional Conversion Programmes (PCP) have been effective in helping workers acquire the skills required and transition into the new jobs created in 2016?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What were the learnings from the current Adapt and Grow initiatives and how have they influenced the enhancements that are being announced in Budget 2017 for CSP and PCP as well as the introduction of the Attach and Train and the Work Trial programmes?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit utilisation
sections.summary: $37 million was allocated last year to training programmes under the SkillsFuture Credit, but only 6% of those eligible had utilised these funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, it allocated $37 million to training programmes under the SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, only 6% out of those eligible had utilised these funds.

sections.label: PMET job vacancies trend
sections.summary: MOM figures show nearly five in 10 job vacancies in 2016 were for PMETs, a trend expected to rise as the economy restructures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Based on MOM's latest figures, in 2016, nearly five in 10 job vacancies in Singapore were for PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: MOM had indicated that this trend is expected to continue to rise as the economy restructures in tandem with the improving skills and education profile of the workforce.

sections.label: Gender gap in STEM jobs
sections.summary: If current gender gap ratios persist from 2015 to 2020, there will be one new STEM job per four jobs lost for men but one per 20 for women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: What this means in absolute terms is that for every three jobs lost for men, one new job is created whereas, for women, there will be more than five jobs lost for every job gained.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: If current gender gap ratios persist over 2015 to 2020, this will mean that there will be one new Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) job per four jobs lost for men, but only one new STEM job per 20 jobs lost for women.

sections.label: MOM scrutiny of weak companies
sections.summary: The question asks whether MOM can update on its scrutiny, engagement with double weak and triple weak companies, and punitive actions on the red lane.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Can MOM provide an update on their additional scrutiny efforts, engagement with "double weak" and "triple weak" companies and the punitive actions on those on the "red lane"?

sections.label: Reservist call-ups and employability
sections.summary: Reservist call-ups disrupt employability, especially in smaller companies, and the Government may consider an incentive scheme for employers of NSmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Disruptions caused by reservist call-ups affect the employability of Singaporeans, especially in companies with fewer staff and less flexible operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Two to three weeks' absence from work could mean poorer performance reviews or even reluctance by employers to hire workers with NS liabilities in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the advanced notice period was meant to give employers a longer runway to re-allocate work, in reality, it does little to mitigate the effects of reservist call-ups since employers will either have to ask other staff to cover the duties of the absent employee, which adds to their workload, or specially hire someone else to cover the worker's duties for that short period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government may want to consider an appropriate incentive scheme to encourage employers to employ NSmen, especially those who still have to fulfil high-key In-Camp Trainings (ICTs).

sections.label: Wages outstripping productivity growth
sections.summary: Between 2011 and 2015 wages outstripped productivity growth every year, with 2015 real median wage growth of 7% against 0.1% productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Between 2011 and 2015, wages outstripped productivity growth in every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, in 2015, real median wage growth was 7%, compared to labour productivity growth of 0.1%.

sections.label: MOM skills and SME support
sections.summary: The question asks how MOM would work with employers and investors on skills, and notes 1,400 SMEs had joined the scheme as of last November.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: How would MOM work with present employers to improve workers' skills, and with would-be investors to develop future skills needed to support the future industries?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It aims to support the growth of SMEs by helping them to develop new capabilities, capacity and markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As of last November, 1,400 SMEs had joined the scheme.

sections.label: LEDS for SME capabilities
sections.summary: The LEDS, focused on helping SMEs develop capabilities, manpower and markets, has been in place since late 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: The LEDS, with its focus to help SMEs develop their capabilities, manpower and markets has been in place since late 2015.

sections.label: P-Max and SME talent
sections.summary: P-Max has been an important part of SMEs' talent pipeline, and the passage asks about progress and beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: What is the progress and how many workers and companies have benefited?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: P-Max has been an important part of SMEs' talent pipeline.

sections.label: Budget Adapt and Grow support
sections.summary: The Government will increase wage and training support under Adapt and Grow schemes and introduce Attach and Train for certain sectors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Government is going to increase wage and training support provided under existing schemes of the Adapt and Grow initiative, as well as introduce an Attach and Train initiative for certain sectors.

sections.label: Attach and Train target companies
sections.summary: The Attach and Train initiative targets companies that are not ready to hire yet.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Attach and Train initiative goes further by targeting companies that are not ready to hire yet.

sections.label: Structured assessment skills figure
sections.summary: A number, while still low, rose to 0.8% in September last year, up 0.2% from September 2015.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A structured assessment of a participating worker's skills condition?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This number, while still low, has risen to 0.8% in September last year, up 0.2% from September 2015.

sections.label: Long-term unemployed PME assistance
sections.summary: The passage asks what more can be done for the long-term unemployed and notes NTUC's U PME centre assisted over 2,500 PMEs since April 2014.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What more can be done to help the long-term unemployed to ensure they are able to find employment within six months of their last job, and stay employed for at least six months in their new job?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could this be attributed to a lack of skills on the part of the jobseekers, or a lack of awareness about available jobs or new skills that they do not know about?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Although we have a relatively low resident unemployment rate of 3.1%, my biggest worry will be for those who are long-term unemployed, especially the PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Since we started in April 2014 until last month, NTUC's U PME centre has assisted more than 2,500 PMEs, out of which 1,350 are for placement assistance.

sections.label: NTUC Career Activation Programme progress
sections.summary: NTUC's U PME Centre started its Career Activation Programme 18 months ago, getting about 20 of 100 participants employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: NTUC's U PME Centre started our Career Activation Programme 18 months ago to do just that and we have achieved positive feedback and steady progress by getting about 20 out of the 100 on our programme employed.

sections.label: PMEs transiting to second careers
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government helps PMEs transit into second careers by exploring job and skill adjacencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: There is strong inertia from many PMEs to explore new industries due to the high opportunity cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: It is with this in mind that I hope the Government can look into helping PMEs transit into second careers more seamlessly by exploring the adjacency of jobs and the adjacency of skills so that these PMEs can move into, move across or move up into new roles which capitalise on their acquired skills and knowledge so that they can even enter mid-career and be given credits for their experience.

sections.label: Employers and mature PMEs
sections.summary: Employers must not discriminate against mature PMEs and must redesign jobs for the shrinking, ageing workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Employers, too, must play their part not to discriminate against mature PMEs and redesign jobs to embrace the tight, shrinking and ageing workforce.

sections.label: CSP qualifying salary too high
sections.summary: Some employers, especially SMEs, said the $4,000 CSP qualifying salary is too high and should be lowered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: First, some employers, especially the SMEs, shared that the $4,000 qualifying salary for CSP is too high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: More middle-age and older workers can benefit if we lower this qualifying salary.

sections.label: Interagency unit for older workers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes an interagency unit to study employability for middle-age and older workers, with tripartite partners adopting differentiated approaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: To provide holistic support for these workers, the tripartite partners must work together to be innovative and adopt differentiated approaches because of our workers' physical and skills requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: I propose to set up an interagency unit to study employability for middle-age and older workers.

sections.label: MOM help for jobless Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker asks how MOM can assist Singaporeans who exhausted means to gain longer term employment, and address redundancies for those aged 40 and above and PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: How can MOM assist Singaporeans, such as Daniel and Saiful, who seem to have exhausted all means to gain longer term employment, despite having post-secondary educational qualifications and substantial work experience?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: How do we address job redundancies, particularly for employees aged 40 and above, and those who are PMEs?

sections.label: MOM PMET job matching
sections.summary: The Minister said MOM matched about 60% of PMETs to jobs last month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: The Minister shared last month that MOM managed to match about 60% of PMETs to jobs.

sections.label: CSP wage cut subsidy
sections.summary: CSP subsidises employers for 12 months to minimise wage cuts for jobseekers hired at $4,000 or more monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: CSP minimises the wage cut by subsidising for 12 months employers who hire such jobseekers in any job that pays a gross salary of at least $4,000 a month.

sections.label: CSP support increase announced
sections.summary: The Finance Minister announced increased wage and training support for CSP, originally set to run until October 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: The Finance Minister announced that the Government will increase wage and training support for CSP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: The CSP initiative was originally intended to run until October 2017.

sections.label: Jobs Bank placement numbers
sections.summary: It asks the number of Singaporeans who found jobs through Jobs Bank yearly since its 2014 inception under the Fair Consideration Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, what is the actual number of Singaporeans who have successfully found jobs through the Jobs Bank in each year since its inception in 2014?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The National Jobs Bank was started as part of the Fair Consideration Framework's mandatory advertising requirement.

sections.label: Jobs Bank salary impression
sections.summary: The Jobs Bank gives the impression its posted jobs are not higher paying, since mandatory advertising covers jobs below $12,000 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Second, the Jobs Bank gives people the impression that the jobs posted there are not for higher paying jobs, since mandatory advertising are for jobs below $12,000 monthly salary.

sections.label: TAFEP enforcement powers urged
sections.summary: The employment claims tribunal is called a good step, and the Ministry is urged to grant TAFEP more enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The latest introduction of the employment claims tribunal introduced last year has been a good step but it only relates to salary disputes for PMETs, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to take the next step and grant TAFEP more enforcement powers to protect the practice of fair employment and non-discriminatory recruitment policies in Singapore, especially in the current frequent changing markets and labour market environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Every company which utilises the funding must commit to sharing productivity gains with our workers.

sections.label: Companies weak on local hiring
sections.summary: The Ministry has developed efforts to place companies on a watchlist for weak commitment to hiring local Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: On the other hand, there were also companies whose hearts were not with our locals, where I received feedback that they use the locals in filling up the numbers and were not particularly interested in developing our local workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: I am pleased that the Ministry has developed efforts to place companies on the watchlist for weak commitment to the hiring of local Singaporeans.

sections.label: Attach and Train programme
sections.summary: The new Attach and Train programme lets workers join companies for training attachments without the firms having to hire them.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The new Attach and Train programme allows workers to join companies for training attachments and the firms do not have to hire them.

sections.label: Fair pay and placement
sections.summary: A speaker asks how to ensure students or workers on the programme are remunerated fairly and placed in a job after training.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As much as we welcome the programme, how can we ensure that students or workers on the programme are remunerated fairly and can be placed in a job after the training?

sections.label: Mandatory retrenchment benefits urged
sections.summary: With 11,890 workers losing jobs in the first nine months of 2016, MOM is urged to reconsider mandatory retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: With an increasing number of workers who have lost their jobs in 2016 − I think it is 11,890 in the first nine months − may I urge MOM to reconsider the need to provide mandatory retrenchment benefits to workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: After all, a recent survey in late 2016 showed that 90.6% of employers do pay retrenchment benefits to workers who were retrenched.

sections.label: Mandatory retrenchment benefit law
sections.summary: The Minister is urged to reconsider a mandatory retrenchment benefit law, as retrenchment rose and unemployment went from 2.8% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I know the Minister has spoken on this topic just last month but allow me to be a little bit more persistent, because workers whose employment is terminated really do not know what their rights are and what they can do to seek fair compensation from their employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, may I urge the Minister to reconsider the need for a mandatory retrenchment benefit law?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Retrenchment has gone up to its highest since the Global Financial Crisis in 2009.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The resident unemployment rate had held steady at about 2.8% for four years since 2012 but went up to 3% last year.

sections.label: Recruitment rate decline
sections.summary: The recruitment rate for companies with 25 or more employees fell from 2.8 new employees per 100 in 2012 to about 2.2 last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The recruitment rate for companies with 25 or more employees has come down, from 2.8 new employees per 100 existing employees in 2012 to about 2.2 last year.

sections.label: local workforce growth
sections.summary: Local workforce growth will never return to the high growth of 2%, 3%, 4% of the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Our local workforce growth will never go back to the high growth of 2%, 3%, 4% of the past.

sections.label: PMET job proportion
sections.summary: The proportion of PMET jobs increased from 49% in 2007 to 55% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The proportion of PMET jobs has increased from 49% in 2007 to 55% last year.

sections.label: productivity improvement
sections.summary: They improved productivity by 35% within the company and across the entire value chain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: As a result, they improved productivity, not just within the company but across the entire value chain, by 35%.

sections.label: companies responding to LEDS
sections.summary: More than 2,000 companies, mostly SMEs across 18 sectors, have responded to LEDS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: More than 2,000 companies, mostly SMEs across 18 sectors, have responded to LEDS.

sections.label: manpower-lean redesign and lift technicians
sections.summary: They will partner companies to redesign workflow to be manpower-lean and offer better jobs, and 1,000 more lift technicians are needed over three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We will partner them to redesign their workflow to be more manpower-lean, and to offer jobs and careers of better qualities to our locals, so that they can compete better for local manpower to support their growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We need 1,000 more lift technicians over the next three years.

sections.label: jobseekers securing jobs
sections.summary: Last year, WSG with NTUC e2i, SNEF and tripartite partners helped more than 20,000 jobseekers secure jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Last year, WSG, together with NTUC e2i, the Singapore National Employers' Federation (SNEF) and our tripartite partners, we helped more than 20,000 jobseekers to secure jobs.

sections.label: National Jobs Bank transformation
sections.summary: The National Jobs Bank will be transformed into a one-stop non-stop online marketplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Our next big move is to transform the entire National Jobs Bank into a one-stop non-stop online marketplace.

sections.label: Partnership for PMET placements
sections.summary: Partners focused on active jobseekers will help place redundant and long-unemployed PMETs, starting in the second quarter, amid rising missed match and mismatch cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: They were selected because of their business focus on active jobseekers, meaning these are the workers who are actively looking for jobs, rather than passive jobseekers where the jobs are looking for the workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We will partner them to help place PMETs who are made redundant and those unemployed for three months or more, and will launch this new partnership in the second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Last year, the number of missed match cases has increased from 14,500 to about 16,000, an increase of about 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: However, the number of mismatch cases has increased even faster, from 3,000 to almost 5,000, an increase of more than 60%.

sections.label: Higher PCP entry support caps
sections.summary: Entry support caps for mid-level PCP jobs will be raised from $2,000 to $4,000 to encourage employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: To encourage employers to offer more PCP jobs at the mid-level, we will raise the entry support caps from $2,000 currently to $4,000.

sections.label: Higher support for mature PMETs
sections.summary: Mature PMETs over 40 or long-term unemployed over six months will receive higher support, increased from $4,000 to $6,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Mature PMETs, who are more than 40 years old, or the long-term unemployed for more than six months, they will continue to receive higher support, an increase from today's $4,000 to $6,000.

sections.label: Training allowances for Attach and Train
sections.summary: Attach and Train trainees will receive training allowances of about 50% to 70% of prevailing salaries, capped at $4,000 monthly, in lieu of employer salary grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked about payment for trainees on the Attach and Train programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We will provide them with training allowances, which are about 50% to 70% of prevailing salaries for the jobs they are being trained for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This will be capped at $4,000 per month, in lieu of salary grants that we pay to the employers.

sections.label: Logistics sector Attach and Train pilot
sections.summary: The logistics sector is being looked at to pilot the Attach and Train programme because it is a key growth sector identified by CFE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Ms Jessica Tan asked which sectors will pilot the Attach and Train programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We are looking at the logistics sector because it is one of the key growth sectors identified by CFE.

sections.label: Wage support for employers
sections.summary: Employers get higher wage support for up to 18 months, and PMETs aged 40-49 get the same support as those aged 50 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Their employers will receive higher wage support and for a longer duration, up from 12 months to 18 months of 50% of wage support for the first six months; 30% for the second six months; and 20% for the last six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In total, the wage support can be as high as $42,000 over 18 months for the employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Second, PMETs aged 40-49, who are made redundant or unemployed for six months, will now get the same level of support as those PMETs aged 50 and above.

sections.label: CSP extension to PMETs
sections.summary: Support rates rise to 40% then 20%, and CSP is extended to all PMETs unemployed six months or more, regardless of age or redundancy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For the first six months, we will increase it from 20% today to 40%; for the next six months, from 10% today to 20%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Third, we will extend CSP to all PMETs who are unemployed for six months or more, regardless of their age, regardless of whether they were made redundant.

sections.label: Lower salary threshold for SMEs
sections.summary: The salary threshold for SMEs is lowered from $4,000 to $3,600 because some SMEs may not meet the qualifying salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: As mentioned by Mr Desmond Choo, the feedback from SMEs is that some may not be able to meet this qualifying salary, especially during this period of weaker growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We, therefore, will lower salary threshold for SMEs, from $4,000 to $3,600.

sections.label: Longer work trial for workers
sections.summary: Work trial for LTU rank-and-file workers is extended from 80 hours to as long as three months, with an allowance of up to $1,200 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Dr Intan Mokhtar will be happy to note that to help more LTU rank-and-file workers to return to work, especially the lower-skilled and lower-wage workers, we have decided to extend the current 80 hours, or two weeks, of work trial to as long as three months, with an allowance of up to $1,200 per month.

sections.label: Jobseeker training and outcomes
sections.summary: A woman took a WSQ healthcare course with transport cost help and now works as a Clinic Assistant; PMET jobseeker outcomes are mixed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, with advice from her career coach, she took up the WSQ Higher Certificate in Healthcare Support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We helped her with transport cost so that she can attend the course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: She missed a few modules when she fell ill, but she persevered to complete the course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Because of her determination and willingness to learn and improve herself, today, she is working as a Clinic Assistant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We have mixed outcomes with PMET jobseekers, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Ms C is highly-qualified, with 10 years of experience in banking and finance.

sections.label: Firms hiring Singaporean PMEs
sections.summary: Firms on the watchlist hired 800 more Singaporean PMEs collectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Collectively, these firms hired 800 more Singaporean PMEs since being placed on our watchlist.

sections.label: Rejected EP applications, curtailed privileges
sections.summary: At TAFEP's recommendation, over 500 EP applications from 50 employers were rejected or withdrawn, and work pass privileges will be curtailed until they improve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: At the recommendation of TAFEP, more than 500 EP applications from these 50 employers have been rejected by MOM or withdrawn by the companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We will continue to curtail their work pass privileges until they improve.

sections.label: Human Capital Partnership programme launch
sections.summary: Last month the Human Capital Partnership programme was launched with 74 employers employing about 100,000 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Last month, we launched the Human Capital Partnership programme with 74 employers employing about 100,000 Singaporeans.

sections.label: Singaporean Core and foreign complementarity
sections.summary: Three commitments: strengthen the Singaporean Core, forge complementarity between local and foreign employees, and strengthen know-how transfer to groom Glocal talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The first is the commitment to strengthen the Singaporean Core by nurturing the "2/3"; second, strengthen the complementarity between local and foreign employees by forging a workplace culture of "2/3" and "1/3", not "2/3" versus "1/3"; and thirdly, strengthening know-how transfer adopting the mindset of "2/3 + 1/3>1" to groom our promising local executives into regional and global executives, or what I call, the Glocal talent, for short.

sections.label: Fast, Normal, Slow Lanes
sections.summary: With the FCF Watchlist and HCP in place, companies will be engaged through Fast Lane, Normal Lane and Slow Lane according to their mindsets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: With the FCF Watchlist and HCP now in place, henceforth, we will adopt a differentiated approach in our engagement of companies. "Fast Lane" for HCP who are progressive employers with the mindset of "2/3 + 1/3>1"; "Normal Lane" for the majority who are fair employers with the mindset of "2/3 and 1/3"; and the "Slow Lane" for FCF Watchlist companies.

sections.label: Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management
sections.summary: TADM was set up to mediate ECT claims; 50 cases were tried, and 80% were resolved successfully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Last year, we also announced the setting up of the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) to mediate the ECT claims, so that only the unsuccessful cases need to be heard at the ECT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We have tried out 50 cases so far involving disputes over termination, training bonds and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We are encouraged that 80% of the cases were resolved successfully.

sections.label: Short-term relief fund
sections.summary: TADM will operate a short-term relief fund to provide quick relief to local low-wage workers owed salary by employers in financial difficulties or business failure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Last but not least, TADM will also operate a short-term relief fund to provide quick relief to local low-wage workers who are owed salary by employers in financial difficulties or business failure.

sections.label: Tripartite standards and NSmen discrimination
sections.summary: The first series of tripartite standards will be launched by the end of the year, and Mr Low Thia Khiang asked about discrimination against NSmen, which is against the Ministry of Defence Enlistment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The first series of tripartite standards will be launched by the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Mr Low Thia Khiang asked about discrimination against NSmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This is against the Ministry of Defence Enlistment Act.

sections.label: Economic growth, retrenchment, unemployment
sections.summary: The speaker relates to how people feel because economic growth has been lower, retrenchment figures higher, and the unemployment rate has gone up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: I can totally relate to how they feel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This is because economic growth has been lower than previous years, while retrenchment figures have been higher than before, and the unemployment rate has gone up.

sections.label: Helping workers and SMEs transform
sections.summary: Tripartite partners will help workers upgrade skills, adopt technology, adjust to new jobs and do well, and help SMEs transform, streamline manpower and maximise resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The tripartite partners will do their best to help workers upgrade their skills, adopt technology, adjust to new jobs constantly and do well in their new career.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We are also committed to help SMEs transform themselves, streamline manpower and maximise the usage of resources, so as to bring value-for-money products and services to both domestic and export markets more quickly.

sections.label: Mutual support and trust
sections.summary: Mutual support and mutual trust with people, workers, unions and businesses have enabled Singapore to emerge from every economic downturn and restructuring stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The mutual support we give to one another, the mutual trust we have built and earned with our people, workers, unions and our businesses has enabled us to emerge from every economic downturn, from every economic restructuring, not weaker, but stronger.

sections.label: Four keys to better careers
sections.summary: The four keys are helping businesses transform and create quality jobs, helping people adapt to new jobs, making the local workforce more inclusive while strengthening local-foreign complementarity, and enhancing employment protection for a fair and progressive workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Together, we can help our businesses to transform and create quality jobs, help our people to adapt to new jobs, make our local workforce more inclusive while strengthening the complementarity in our local-foreign workforce and, lastly, enhance our employment protection framework for a fair and progressive workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, these are the four keys to a future of better careers for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We know what we need to do and we are working in unity to get there ahead of all the others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Let us transform and grow together to create growth in our economy, adapt and grow together to create good jobs, better careers for all our people to live a better life.

sections.label: Foreign construction worker recruitment costs
sections.summary: A foreign construction worker typically pays about S$15,000 in recruitment costs, and with basic salaries around $600 a month cannot save enough during a 12-month Work Permit to recover this sum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A foreign construction worker looking for his first job in Singapore typically pays about S$15,000 as recruitment costs, a result of recruitment channels placed in the hands of the few who go out to maximise profits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When basic salaries are around $600 a month, no workers can expect to save enough during the 12 months' duration of a typical Work Permit to recover this sum.

sections.label: Work Permit holders repatriation rule
sections.summary: Work Permit holders must be repatriated before they can seek alternative employment in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Work Permit holders cannot seek alternative employment in Singapore without first being repatriated.

sections.label: Change of Employer permissions
sections.summary: MOM granted Change of Employer permission to 2,200 workers in three years, a fraction of salary complaints raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOM has said "Change of Employer" permission were granted to 2,200 workers in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But this is only a fraction of the salary complaints workers have raised which, at 4,500 per year, would be 13,500 over the last three years.

sections.label: Companies signed up with LEDS
sections.summary: 2,100 companies have signed up with LEDS and are being helped to cross the technology gate towards the market gate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: To date, 2,100 companies have signed up with LEDS and we are helping them to take steps to cross, especially the technology gate towards the market gate.

sections.label: LEDS jobs and wage increases
sections.summary: Nearly 10,000 good jobs are expected from SPRING-supported firms under LEDS, with an average 18% wage increase for redesigned roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Based on our analysis, nearly 10,000 good jobs are expected to be created by firms supported by SPRING under LEDS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: For a scheme that has been about one year old so far, there is an average of 18% wage increase for those whose roles were redesigned or upgraded through LEDS projects supported by NTUC-e2i.

sections.label: Order to serving time cut
sections.summary: Time from ordering to serving was cut by 40%, table turnover is faster, and customer satisfaction and customer base increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: The time taken from ordering to serving has been cut by 40%, table turnover is faster, customer satisfaction has increased and their customer base has expanded, too.

sections.label: P-Max programme 2016 figures
sections.summary: Almost 1,100 SMEs were supported and 1,200 PMETs placed under the P-Max programme in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Mr Desmond Choo will be pleased to know that almost 1,100 SMEs were supported and 1,200 PMETs were placed under the P-Max programme in 2016.

sections.label: Payroll software for salary disputes
sections.summary: A solution integrating with third-party payroll software helps avoid salary disputes on working hours, and 90 SMEs have adopted it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: This solution can also help workers avoid salary disputes on working hours as it can be customised to integrate with any third-party payroll software, ensuring seamless transference of working hours for the employers to compute the salary payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that 90 SMEs have adopted this solution.

sections.label: Inventory and manpower savings
sections.summary: Companies can reduce excess inventory holding from 30% to 15% and achieve 10% manpower savings as fewer workers do stocktaking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: With this solution, companies can expect to reduce their excess inventory holding from 30% to 15% and achieve manpower savings of 10% as fewer workers are required to conduct stocktaking of the excess inventory items.

sections.label: 71 solutions across 17 industries
sections.summary: There are currently 71 solutions, some off-the-shelf, spread across 17 industries to be pushed out and made pervasive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Currently, we have 71 solutions, some off-the-shelf, spread across 17 industries that we are going to push out and make pervasive.

sections.label: Manpower flexibility for solution providers
sections.summary: Manpower flexibility is granted only to solution providers who can scale up, have demand, and considered Singaporeans, targeting 2,400 companies this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: We need to enable those companies that provide these solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: This flexibility in manpower will only be granted to solution providers who have demonstrated to us that they can scale up and, at the same time, there is demand for their solutions and that they have also considered Singaporeans for these job opportunities before we allow for such manpower flexibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: We are targeting at 2,400 companies this year alone and we want the sector to change, and we want it to be pervasive across all sectors.

sections.label: Foreign workers with salary claims
sections.summary: MOM will help foreign workers with valid salary non-payment claims, allowing them to change employer and stay even if their work pass is terminated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: For foreign workers with valid claims of salary non-payment, MOM will help them see through their claim and allow them to change employer and stay on in Singapore, even if their employer terminates their work pass.

sections.label: Caps on employment agency costs
sections.summary: Laws already cap costs charged by employment agencies to foreign workers at a maximum of two months of their salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Our laws today already cap the costs that will be charged by the employment agencies to foreign workers to two months maximum or capped at two months of their salary.

sections.label: Work injury compensation for foreign workers
sections.summary: Foreign workers today receive compensation for work injuries under WICA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Foreign workers today receive compensation for work injuries under WICA.

sections.label: Migrant Workers' Assistance Fund
sections.summary: MWC aids workers using the Migrant Workers' Assistance Fund, set up in 2012, which can provide more assistance like a relief fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: MWC's aid to the workers is provided using the Migrant Workers' Assistance Fund (MWAF).

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: This Fund was set up in 2012 and more assistance can come out of the Fund to help the workers like a relief fund.

sections.label: Dormitory amenities and licensing compliance
sections.summary: Workers have access to dormitory amenities such as ATMs, canteens and mini-marts; 48 of 50 large dormitories are licensed and over 70% of inspected FCDs comply with new requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: They also have access to recreational areas and amenities, such as automated teller machines (ATMs), canteens and mini-marts, all within their dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: So far, 48 out of 50 large dormitories have been licensed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: While the new requirements were put in place only in January this year, over 70% of these FCDs inspected already comply with these standards.

sections.label: FDW salary records and electronic payment
sections.summary: Employers must keep monthly salary records and pay FDWs electronically on request; the government supports electronic payment efforts and will work with partners to ensure fair treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Our employers are required to maintain a record of the monthly salary paid to FDWs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Employers are also required to pay the FDWs' salary electronically if she so requests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Some FDWs may prefer to be paid in cash and to avoid being charged a fee if their bank accounts fall below the minimum sum required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: But we are open to Mr Louis Ng's idea and we also support CDE's push for electronic payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: It is heartening to note that CDE is currently working with some banks to help FDWs set up bank accounts more easily and with better returns and we will help to facilitate that and support them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: We will continue to work with the employers, employment agencies, non-government organisations (NGOs) like MWC and CDE, to ensure that these foreign workers can work safely and be treated fairly during their stay in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: However, broader adoption is tepid because of mindset, manpower and operational constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Mrs Josephine Teo's pilot announced on 2 March is an important step to broader adoption at the sectoral level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: I am glad that MOM will go beyond the Tripartite Advisory and develop tripartite standards for companies to answer the clarion call.

sections.label: WorkPro and Job Redesign Toolkit
sections.summary: WorkPro was enhanced with grants for age management practices and workplace redesign, and a Job Redesign Toolkit was launched by MOM, SNEF and NTUC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: WorkPro was enhanced in making grants to help companies implement age management practices and redesign workplaces and processes for older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, a Job Redesign Toolkit for companies developed by MOM, SNEF and NTUC was launched.

sections.label: Agency fees and illegal kickbacks
sections.summary: There is a bondage of exorbitant agency fees and illegal kickbacks, with about 12,000 cleaning companies engaging about 58,000 cleaners as of 31 September 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: A bondage with exorbitant agency fees and illegal kickbacks that they have to pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: There are about 12,000 cleaning companies engaging about 58,000 cleaners, both local and foreign, as of 31 September 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: A $3,000 kickback per foreign worker will translate into some serious money even if just 10% of the cleaning workforce were subject to the abuse.

sections.label: Enforcement of workers' rights
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will share results and efforts to tackle disregard for the law and workers' rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry share its results and efforts to effectively tackle such blatant disregard for the law and basic workers' rights?

sections.label: Changes to WIS
sections.summary: Last year's Budget made four changes to WIS, including a higher income ceiling and monthly payments, but did not raise the cash component.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: During last year's Budget, changes were made to WIS in order to "provide a more direct and timely reward for work effort and ensure that WIS continues to provide a meaningful level of support for eligible workers." There were four main changes, including a higher qualifying income ceiling, slightly higher payouts, monthly payments instead of quarterly and increased contributions to CPF, MediSave and the Special Account.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: The Government, however, stopped short of increasing the cash component of WIS from the current 40%.

sections.label: Reviewing the PWM
sections.summary: The passage says it is time to review the PWM, and NTUC will work with tripartite partners on annual increments and bonuses.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Mr Zainal Sapari, please take your two cuts together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, this year, I believe it is time for us to review the PWM to ensure that it remains relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: NTUC will be working with our tripartite partners in the various sectoral committees for annual increments and annual bonuses to be incorporated as part of PWM, in particular, the Security and Landscape sectors.

sections.label: Workplace deaths last year
sections.summary: The passage states that sixty-six lives were lost at the workplace last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Sixty-six lives were lost at the workplace last year.

sections.label: bizSAFE levels and RMAF
sections.summary: The passage sets out bizSAFE level timelines for companies and hopes the Ministry will consider bringing back the RMAF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Companies should obtain their bizSAFE level one within the first year of operation, acquire bizSAFE level two in the next two years and reach bizSAFE level three in the following three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As SMEs may find it challenging to get accredited, I hope that the Ministry will consider bringing back the Risk Management Assistance Funding (RMAF) to assist these companies.

sections.label: Re-employment age raised
sections.summary: The re-employment age will be raised to 67 from 1 July this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The re-employment age will be raised to 67 from 1 July this year to allow our growing pool of older workers to contribute to the workforce for as long as they can.

sections.label: WorkPro Job Redesign funding increase
sections.summary: Companies can now receive up to $300,000, up from $150,000, to redesign jobs for older workers under the WorkPro Job Redesign scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: A company can now receive funding of up to $300,000, up from $150,000, to redesign jobs for older workers under the WorkPro Job Redesign scheme.

sections.label: New foreign worker salary threshold
sections.summary: The Ministry will raise the salary threshold to $1,100 from 1 July this year and to $1,200 from 1 July next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: If not, it means that we are gradually loosening our foreign worker controls simply due to rising nominal wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: So, given the rising income levels, my Ministry has decided to adopt a new salary threshold of $1,200.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: This will be done in two steps: first, to $1,100 from 1 July this year and, next, to $1,200 from 1 July next year.

sections.label: Cleaners' median wage growth
sections.summary: After the cleaning PWM announcement, median gross wages for full-time resident cleaners grew 12% per annum from 2012 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: After the announcement of the cleaning PWM, median gross wages for full-time resident cleaners grew by 12% per annum from 2012 to 2015.

sections.label: Annual bonus for resident cleaners
sections.summary: From 2020 onwards, all resident cleaners will receive an annual bonus equivalent to two weeks of basic monthly wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: All resident cleaners will also receive an annual bonus equivalent to two weeks of basic monthly wages from 2020 onwards.

sections.label: Updated Tripartite Advisory on Best Sourcing
sections.summary: The second prong to help low-wage workers is stepping up best sourcing efforts, with the updated Tripartite Advisory on Best Sourcing Practices released today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Our second prong to help low-wage workers is to step up our best sourcing efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce the release of the updated Tripartite Advisory on Best Sourcing Practices today.

sections.label: Higher WIS income cap and payouts
sections.summary: The WIS income cap was raised so workers earning up to $2,000 can receive WIS payouts of up to $3,600 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: First, we have raised the WIS income cap so that workers earning up to $2,000 are now able to receive WIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Workers can now receive higher WIS payouts of up to $3,600 per year.

sections.label: WIS enhancements for low-wage workers
sections.summary: This round of WIS enhancements will benefit more than 460,000 low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: More than 460,000 low-wage workers will benefit from this round of WIS enhancements.

sections.label: Workplace fatality rate and deaths
sections.summary: The workplace fatality rate stayed at 1.9 per 100,000 for two years, with 66 deaths in 2016 dropping to 24 in the second half of last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Our workplace fatality rate stayed at 1.9 per 100,000 employed persons for the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: In 2016, as pointed out by Mr Melvin Yong, 66 workers lost their lives at work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Through concerted efforts by our industry partners and also our stepped-up enforcement and engagement, the number of fatalities dropped to 24 in the second half of last year.

sections.label: Construction sector top fatalities contributor
sections.summary: The construction sector remained the top contributor with 24 fatalities in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The construction sector remained the top contributor with 24 fatalities in 2016.

sections.label: MOM action on WSH breaches
sections.summary: MOM will act on the company and hold senior management responsible and accountable if their actions breach the WSH Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: MOM will take actions not only on the company but also hold the senior management responsible and accountable if their actions breach the WSH Act.

sections.label: Survey on freelancer profiles
sections.summary: Minister Lim Swee Say told the House his Ministry is looking into results of a new survey on freelancer profiles in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
sentences.text: Last month, Minister Lim Swee Say told the House that his Ministry is looking into results of a new survey commissioned to enable the Government to better understand the profiles of freelancers in Singapore.

sections.label: Freelancers share of workforce
sections.summary: Freelancers make up about close to 10% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Freelancers make up about close to 10% of the workforce.

sections.label: MOM freelancer survey and task force
sections.summary: The speaker looks forward to MOM's survey on freelancing trends and notes a task force is being formed for freelancers' concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I look forward to the results of the survey by MOM which will reveal changes and trends in the freelancing landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was also announced earlier that the Ministry is forming a task force to address the concerns faced by freelancers.

sections.label: Tharman on gig economy risk
sections.summary: Tharman said the gig economy warrants a closer look and warned of drift-risk passed from companies to workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Tharman himself was so concerned about the gig economy that he has said that the issue warrants a closer look.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And he said at the McKinsey Innovation Forum recently that, "We have got to avoid a continuing drift-risk being passed from companies to workers, who actually cannot take much risk − the risk of instability in wages and the risk of not being prepared for retirement because of a lack of social security contributions." Even as our economy evolves, young Singaporeans should think carefully and not be lulled into thinking that freelancing in the gig economy will help secure their future.

sections.label: Portability of medical insurance benefits
sections.summary: The passage states that portability of medical insurance benefits is one particular area of concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One particular area of concern is the portability of medical insurance benefits.

sections.label: Tax deductions and portable medical insurance
sections.summary: The Ministry offers higher tax deductions to employers paying into portable medical insurance, and the speaker proposes an employee option to keep benefits at own expense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Ministry is offering companies higher tax deductions to employers who pay into their employees' portable medical insurance benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In order to ensure that there is no additional cost to the employer, I would like to propose that the Ministry provide an option for the employee to continue to keep his existing benefits with his existing company under his own expense.

sections.label: Employee option to continue insurance
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that departing employees may pay $1,000 at their own expense to continue existing benefits without lapse or new underwriting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, as long as the employee is employed by the company, the company pays for him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But once he leaves his job, he should be given the option of paying $1,000 at his own expense to continue with his existing benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The insurance provider continues to provide the insurance without any lapse, and there is no need for new underwriting because the employee would have been under continuous coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I hope that the Ministry can consider this proposal.

sections.label: Growth of independent workers
sections.summary: The McKinsey Global Institute reported that the segment of independent workers is growing fast at 30% a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The McKinsey Global Institute reported that this segment of independent workers is growing fast, at 30% a year.

sections.label: Gig economy labour law rethink
sections.summary: The passage calls for urgent government action to rethink labour laws and establish CPF contribution obligations for contracts for service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: If we expect the gig economy to prevail in Singapore' future, then the Government must take urgent action to rethink labour laws in order to accord freelance, self-employed individuals an appropriate level of support and rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, establish CPF contribution obligations for parties entering into a contract for service.

sections.label: CPF Investment Scheme returns
sections.summary: The passage states $24 billion is invested in CPFIS, which is deemed unfit for purpose, with 84% of investors not realising higher returns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Twenty-four billion dollars have already been invested in the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS), yet it is deemed to be "unfit for purpose".

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Eighty-four percent of CPFIS investors did not realise higher returns from their investments than they would have received had they left it in their CPF Ordinary Account, risk-free, whilst a substantial number actually suffered losses.

sections.label: Costly courses and conferences
sections.summary: The passage lists answers including the Cambridge Advanced Leadership programme, Organisational Development, language immersions and tech conferences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some answers included the Cambridge Advanced Leadership programme that costs about $30,000, Organisational Development in the US and UK that costs $13,000, Intensive Language and Cultural Immersions in Lebanon and Beijing, costly tech conferences in Silicon Valley and so on.

sections.label: Broadening CPF education loan scheme
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to consider broadening the loan scheme for working professionals pursuing costly modular international courses or conferences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, many of the controls written into it currently are designed around those intentions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that this is why the scheme currently only supports loans for full-time, subsidised diploma courses or degree courses conducted locally at approved educational institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister consider broadening the loan scheme, so that it can enable working professionals to have another liquidity option to tap on if they want to pursue a short but costly cutting-edge modular international course or conference?

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am well aware that there is a legitimate worry about the jeopardising of retirement funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I believe controls similar to those existing ones in the schemes, such as a cap on the amount of withdrawal or duration of return of funds can be factored in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I believe that this will help Singaporeans who wish to pursue the call to go out to learn from the best in the world on how to innovate and internationalise and quite willing to use their own money to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In 2013, about six in 10 active members turning 55 met the Basic Retirement Sum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We expect this proportion to increase to seven in 10 for members turning 55 years old in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: To help CPF members to save more for their retirement, we made several enhancements last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We raised the CPF salary ceiling from $5,000 to $6,000.

sections.label: Older workers CPF contribution rates
sections.summary: The passage states about 570,000 workers aged 50 and above benefited from the increase in CPF contribution rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: About 570,000 workers aged 50 and above benefited from the increase in our CPF contribution rates.

sections.label: Members receiving cash top-ups
sections.summary: The passage states 49,000 members received cash top-ups of $860 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Forty-nine thousand members received cash top-ups of $860 million.

sections.label: Lowering sales charge cap
sections.summary: The passage states the lowering of the cap on sales charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Second, the lowering of the cap on sales charge.

sections.label: CPF LRIS for members
sections.summary: CPF members who prefer a simpler investment option can look forward to CPF LRIS being worked on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For CPF members who prefer a simpler investment option, they can look forward to CPF LRIS that we are working on.

sections.label: Three CPF plan options
sections.summary: From January 2018, CPF members will have three options: Standard, Basic and Escalating Plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: With this new option, from January next year, January 2018, CPF members will have three options: Standard and Basic Plans and now the Escalating Plan.

sections.label: Extending CPF Retirement Planning Service
sections.summary: The CPF Retirement Planning Service will be extended to all CPF members turning age 54 this year, with about 20,000 invited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: As members have found this service useful, therefore, we will extend the CPF Retirement Planning Service to all CPF members turning age 54 this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: An estimate of about 20,000 of them will be invited.

sections.label: Primary freelancers number flat
sections.summary: The total number of primary freelancers remained flat at about 167,000 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: First, the total number of primary freelancers remains flat at about 167,000 in 2016.

sections.label: Total freelancers with secondary
sections.summary: Adding secondary freelancers, the total number of freelancers in Singapore would be about 200,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Second, if we add the secondary freelancers, then the total number of freelancers in Singapore would be about 200,000.

sections.label: Freelancing as preferred choice
sections.summary: About 81% of freelancers do freelancing as a preferred choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Thirdly, about 81% of freelancers do freelancing as a preferred choice.

sections.label: Gig worker groups and numbers
sections.summary: Groups with more than 1,000 include professional, creative, media and communications services, plus 10,000 private hire car workers, totalling about 20,000 gig workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Among those with more than 1,000, we have professional services, including consultants, accountants and bookkeepers; creative services: graphic designers, interior designers and product designers; media and communications: producers, editors and photographers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, 10,000 in the private hire car, plus 10,000 from the rest of the groups, and if we put them all together, that would be about 20,000 gig workers we have today.

sections.label: Tripartite workgroup on freelancers
sections.summary: A tripartite workgroup will be formed to study issues and find solutions for freelancers' well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In consultation with our tripartite partners, we will form a tripartite workgroup to study these issues, address the concerns of the freelancers and come up with workable solutions for the well-being of the freelancing workforce in our future economy.

sections.label: Monitoring freelancer landscape survey
sections.summary: The first survey gives insights into Singapore's freelancer landscape, and developments will be monitored with tripartite partners to find practical solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The first survey is a good starting point for us to get better insights into the freelancer landscape in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor the developments and, together with our tripartite partners, we will find practical solutions to address the issues faced by the freelancers.

sections.label: No employer-employee relationship for trainees
sections.summary: Trainees selected by the industry body will go through training as trainees, so there is no employment and no employer-employee relationship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: With that in mind, on the first question about whether there will be an employer-employee relationship, the answer is no.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: These trainees will be selected by the industry body, and then they will go through the training as trainees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, there is no employment and there is no employer-employee relationship.

sections.label: Launching schemes and hiring obligation
sections.summary: Schemes would be launched when there is demand, with the obligation to hire placed on the industry partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Therefore, as and when there is a demand, I would be happy to launch them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We are putting the obligation to hire on the industry partner.

sections.label: Placement responsibility after training
sections.summary: At the end of training, the industry partner is responsible for finding placement, supported by WSG and e2i.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: At the same time, at the end of the training, the responsibility to find placement would likewise rest with our industry partner, supported by WSG and e2i.

sections.label: Female STEM graduates proportion
sections.summary: The proportion of female university fresh graduates in STEM courses rose from 37% to more than 40%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: If I remember correctly, broadly, the proportion of female university fresh graduates in STEM courses has gone up from 37% to more than 40%.

sections.label: Technology, inclusive economy, leadership grooming
sections.summary: Faster technology use helps move to an innovation-driven future economy and make jobs easier, safer and smarter for all workers, including low-wage and older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The faster we make use of technology, the better hope we have in terms of not just moving into the future economy, which is driven by innovation and technology, but, more importantly, to use technology to make the job of all workers, for example, low-wage workers and older workers, easier, safer, smarter, so that the future economy can, likewise, be an inclusive economy for our workers, both male and female.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: I understand that the Government intends to groom 800 potential leaders in the next three years under the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative (LDI) which was announced in the Budget Statement.

sections.label: Construction worksite coordination and fatalities
sections.summary: Lack of workplace coordination, especially at construction sites, led to injuries and fatalities, with 24 construction fatalities last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: First, is on the lack of coordination at workplaces, particularly the construction sites, that has led to many worksite injuries and fatalities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: That is why the construction sector continued to be the major contributor with 24 fatalities last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: My Ministry will be working with the WSH Council to review the WSH (Construction) Regulations to require construction worksites to hold daily meetings, particularly when they have major hazardous activities to be performed.

sections.label: Snap@MOM unsafe work reporting app
sections.summary: MOM developed a mobile app, Snap@MOM, letting anyone with a smart phone report unsafe work conditions or practices to MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: In this respect, MOM has developed a mobile app called Snap@MOM which made it easier for anyone who has a smart phone to report unsafe work conditions or practices to MOM.

sections.label: Upgrading Snap@MOM for companies
sections.summary: MOM wants companies to download Snap@MOM onto their systems so workers can report near miss incidents to management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: As a result, we were able to prevent worksite accidents from happening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: We want to further upgrade this platform by allowing companies to download this app onto their system so that they can integrate this Snap@MOM throughout the whole company, so that every worker will be able to report near miss incidents to their management.

sections.label: Success rate and LTU group
sections.summary: The success rate is seven out of 10, with 30% unsuccessful, and a small LTU group is the main concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Our success rate today is seven out of 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: There are still 30% who have not been successful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Our main concern is that among them, there is a small group, the LTU group.

sections.label: Standard PCP with sectors
sections.summary: The arrangement with the various sectors is that there is a standard PCP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The answer is yes, our arrangement with the various sectors is that we have a standard PCP.

sections.label: Major initiative launch timing
sections.summary: Movement has started fast, with a major initiative to be launched by the middle of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In fact, we have started moving quite fast.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We are going to launch some major initiative by the middle of this year.

sections.label: Slowing workforce and Adapt and Grow
sections.summary: Local workforce growth is slowing to 1%, companies face challenges finding workers, and Adapt and Grow addresses worker and employer needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Our local workforce growth is slowing down to 1%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: More and more companies, like what Mr Thomas Chua mentioned earlier, are not only having problems finding customers, they are also having challenges finding workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: With Adapt and Grow, we believe that we are not just satisfying the employment needs of the workers but, at the same time, also looking after the manpower needs of the employers.

sections.label: Fair treatment and tripartite assurance
sections.summary: Fair and progressive treatment may make workers more engaged and motivated, and tripartite partners will be pro-worker and pro-business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: If the workers are treated fairly, treated progressively, hopefully, they will become more engaged, more motivated and thereby do better for the business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, I assure Miss Cheryl Can and all Members in this House that everything we do as tripartite partners would be both pro-worker and pro-business.

sections.label: Withdrawal of amendment
sections.summary: The speaker begs leave to withdraw the amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: With that, Madam, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
